newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-PETRENKO HITS GOAL AFTER 16 SECONDS.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-PETRENKO HITS GOAL AFTER 16 SECONDS.

text.p: Sergei Petrenko scored one of the quickest opening goals ever in the world ice hockey championship in the 16th second but Russia were still held to a 2-2 draw by Slovakia on Sunday.
After Petrenko's shock opener on a rebound off Slovak goalkeeper Jaromir Dragan, Russia went nearly 52 minutes before scoring again.
"We got off to an easy start, perhaps it was too easy and that affected our game," Russia head coach Igor Dimitryev said.
Slovakia scored two half-lucky goals in the second period, with Russian netminder Maxim Mikhailovsky seeming only half awake each time.
In the 31st minute, centre forward Jozef Dano lightly touched the puck by the near post and Mikhailovsky fumbled it into the net to level the scores.
Seven minutes later, winger Zdenko Ciger put the Slovaks ahead with a loose shot from a distance, definitely a mistake by the Russian keeper, although his line of vision was briefly blocked.
"We will not send him (Mikhailovsky) away behind the Ural mountains," Dimitryev joked. "I don't want to blame him for the mistakes," he added.
Ciger sat in the penalty box when Andrei Skopintsev whipped in the equaliser halfway through the last period on a smart pass from behind the goal by Denis Afinogenov.
The draw was the first surprise result of the tournament and may hurt Russia's chances of finishing among the top three teams in group A who will go through to the final stage.
